title: Structural insights into RNA phosphorylation by the RNase PNK module of the human rixosome complex.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed both deposited atomic models from the Protein Data Bank (PDB): 10RR (1.4 MB mmCIF, 10,302 atom records, 5 molecular entities including a 3-nucleotide RNA) and 10RN (1.2 MB mmCIF, 9,838 atom records, 4 entities). Read the article's data availability statement on PubMed Central, which lists exactly these 2 models and 6 cryo-electron microscopy density maps, and confirmed the only supplementary file is a 14 MB PDF of figures. Confirmed in the PDB that both entries cite this paper.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The biochemical findings (XRN2, a 5'-to-3' exoribonuclease, preferentially degrading NOL9-phosphorylated RNA; reconstitution of the complex) come from the abstract and the data availability statement only — Europe PMC returned HTTP 500 for the full text, so the gel-based assays were read about, not inspected. No numeric assay table exists to inspect in any case.

a1_downloadable.note: Verified: both mmCIF models download freely from the PDB with no login; the six maps are public in the Electron Microscopy Data Bank (EMDB).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no table at all, so no label column. The deposited data are 2 atomic coordinate files and 6 density maps; any machine-learning target (phosphorylation site, RNA accommodation, binding affinity) would have to be constructed from scratch across other sources.

a3_inputs_present.note: Verified in the mmCIF files: full protein and RNA sequences and 3-D coordinates are present, not just accession references. But for only 2 structures.

a4_units_stated.note: Coordinates in angstroms and reported resolutions (3.5 A for 10RR, 3.6 A for 10RN) are standard and stated in the files; no assay units to check because there is no assay table.

a5_enough_rows.note: Verified: 2 atomic models and 6 maps. The checklist floor is ~1,500 labelled rows (~400 for classification). Treating each atom as a row is not a legitimate unit of analysis here; the experimental unit is the structure, n=2.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~2.6 MB for both mmCIF files; density maps are a few hundred MB each if fetched
a6_fits_laptop.note: Verified file sizes locally; size is not the problem.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Verified: the data availability statement lists 2 PDB entries and 6 EMDB maps, and exactly those exist in the PDB with matching ligands (ATP-gamma-S; AMP-PNP plus rCAA RNA).

a8_label_provenance.note: Not applicable because no label exists. The nearest candidate signals (modelled RNA position, side-chain placement) are themselves human/automated model-building outputs fitted into density, i.e. derived from a model rather than an independent measurement.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: with two structures and no measured outcome column, nothing can be trained or honestly evaluated on this paper's data.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use RNA and protein sequence to predict where an RNA-processing enzyme adds a phosphate group.
plain_idea.train_on: Considered: the structures of human RNase PNK (a four-protein assembly of two LAS1L nuclease subunits and two NOL9 kinase subunits) with bound nucleotides and RNA. Verified count: 2 atomic models, 6 density maps.
plain_idea.predict: Considered: which RNA 5' ends get phosphorylated, or how tightly RNA sits in the kinase active site. The true answer would come from gel-based enzyme assays, which this paper reports only as images, not as numbers.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Ribosome-biogenesis and heterochromatin researchers would use a predictor of rixosome RNA targets, but this paper supplies no measurements to train one on.
plain_idea.verdict_note: Stated for completeness; the project is not well defined on this data.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper. The deposited content is two cryo-electron microscopy structures of the human RNase PNK module plus six density maps; it contains no feature/label table, no quantitative assay output, and no repeated measurements. At most these two coordinate files could serve as a single test case inside a much larger protein-RNA structure or interface-prediction benchmark assembled from the whole PDB, which is a different project with a different data source.

effort.compute_note: Measured the two downloaded mmCIF files (1.2 and 1.4 MB). No modelling estimates are meaningful because there is no training set.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the deposited rows: the data availability statement names 2 atomic models and 6 maps, which I confirmed in the PDB in under five minutes. That alone kills it.

verdict_reason: Structural biology paper whose entire dataset is 2 cryo-EM atomic models (verified: 10RR with 10,302 atoms, 10RN with 9,838) plus 6 density maps and a 14 MB figure PDF. Fails A2 (no label column exists anywhere) and A5 (n=2 experimental units versus the ~1,500-row floor); the biochemistry is reported as gel images with no numeric table.
